rationale:
The reviewed tests adequately check `requirements.sdk.outlines.Span`.

**Indexing semantics.** `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[span_indexes_str_at_utf8_byte_boundaries]` uses the source "aé🦀", which is 7 bytes long.
- It asserts `&source[Span::new(1, 3)] == "é"`. This covers an inclusive start, an exclusive end and multi-byte characters.
- It asserts that `Span::new(7, 7)` gives `""`. This is an empty span at the end boundary, with `end == len`.
- It asserts that each of these spans panics:
  - `Span::new(2, 3)`: the start is not a character boundary.
  - `Span::new(0, 2)`: the end is not a character boundary.
  - `Span::new(2, 2)`: both offsets are off boundary.
  - `Span::new(0, 8)`: the end is greater than `source.len()`.
  - `Span::new(3, 1)`: `start > end`.
- Together these cover each clause of "valid span" and the "same bounds and boundary checks" as range slicing. They also exercise `Index<Span> for str` and `Span::new`.

**Offsets from the original snapshot, including nested items.**
- `fn[unicode_spans_use_bytes_and_whitespace_only_lines_create_no_items]` asserts exact byte spans for the root and for nested line items after multi-byte characters. For example, 🦀 sits at `Span::new(6, 10)`. It also asserts that `&source[item.span]` equals the item text.
- `fn[setext_sections_inside_directives_lists_and_quotes_retain_container_spans]` checks nested Markdown sections inside directives, lists and quotes. It asserts `item.span.start`, `name_span` and `selected.text() == &source[item.span]` against the original source, with non-ASCII text.
- Both tests cover the "original source snapshot, including when a caller selects a nested item" clause.

**Type shape and trait implementations.**
- Public fields and `Span::new` are used in many other tests in `outline_content.rs`.
- `Copy`, `PartialEq` and `Debug` are exercised through `.map(|item| item.span)` on a borrowed item and through `assert_eq!` on spans.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/public_api.rs#fn[check_declaration]`, run from `fn[public_exports_match_the_appendix]`, compares the requirement's declaration and trait-impl listing with rustdoc output. That listing covers `Clone`, `Copy`, `Eq`, `PartialEq`, `Debug` and `Index<Span> for str`. The check also requires `#[non_exhaustive]` on structs with public fields. It would catch a missing `Eq` or `Clone` impl, or a missing `non_exhaustive`.

I found no untested obligation and no wrong expected result. There are no acknowledgments.

text: `trust_but_verify::outline::Span` locates text by byte offsets from the start
of the original source snapshot, including when a caller selects a nested item.
`start` is inclusive and `end` is exclusive. A valid span satisfies
`start <= end <= source.len()` and both offsets are UTF-8 character boundaries.
For `source: &str`, `&source[span]` yields the same slice as
`&source[span.start..span.end]`, with the same bounds and boundary checks.
pub fn new(start: usize, end: usize) -> Self;
